Dear [Resident],

Thank you for reaching out, and I understand why heavy rain still puts you on edge — the 2022 flooding that damaged 17 homes in Willow Glen was serious, and I don't want to minimize that.

I want to give you a direct and honest answer: **no, the Cedar Creek project will not provide additional flood protection to Willow Glen this winter.** Here's why:

- The project has two phases. Phase 1, in the downtown reach, is complete and performing well — that stretch is now rated for a 25-year flood event, and minor flooding at the downtown gauge is down significantly since it finished in 2024.
- **Phase 2, which covers Willow Glen and Fairmont**, is the phase that would protect your neighborhood specifically (levee setbacks and storm-drain upgrades). That phase **has not started construction**. Only 4 of the 11 needed easements have closed, and current engineering projections put substantial completion at **February 2028** — well over a year behind the original schedule. There has been public discussion about accelerating this to fall 2027, but our county engineers rate that as high-risk and not achievable under current funding and crew levels, so I don't want to promise you a date we can't stand behind.
- The project is also running about $4.2M over its original bond authorization, which is part of why acceleration is difficult without additional funding decisions by the Board.

The good news, if there is any, is that the last two winters were 35–40% below normal rainfall, which is likely why we haven't seen major flood damage claims recently — but that's a function of drought, not flood protection, and engineering staff are clear that it doesn't reflect how the neighborhood would fare in a normal or heavy rain year.

In the meantime, I'd strongly encourage you to:
- Use the **sandbag distribution depots** (three locations countywide) if heavy rain is forecast this season — I can send you the nearest location and hours.
- Sign up for county flood alerts if you haven't already, so you get advance notice ahead of storms.
- Consider flood insurance if you don't already carry it, even outside the mapped high-risk zone, given your street's history.

I know this isn't the answer you were hoping for. I'll continue pushing for Phase 2 progress and will keep you updated as easement acquisitions and construction milestones move forward. Please don't hesitate to reach out with any other questions.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
District 3 Office
